task.goal: Build `wordfreq`, a small Node.js command-line tool that prints the N most frequent words in a text file, with tests and a README. Use only the Node.js standard library.
task.result: The final test cleanup is complete: the duplicate root test and accidental root fixture were removed, and the remaining suite matches the documented Unicode/apostrophe tokenization behavior. `npm test` passes with all 7 tests.

sessions.brief: Build `wordfreq`, a small Node.js command-line tool that prints the N most frequent words in a text file, with tests and a README. Use only the Node.js standard library.
sessions.result: The final test cleanup is complete: the duplicate root test and accidental root fixture were removed, and the remaining suite matches the documented Unicode/apostrophe tokenization behavior. `npm test` passes with all 7 tests.

sessions.brief: Implement the Node.js CLI wordfreq in owned files only: create package setup and executable/source (e.g. package.json and wordfreq.js). Requirements: stdlib only; CLI accepts a text file and N, counts words case-insensitively, prints top N by descending frequency with deterministic alphabetical ties; validation/usage errors to stderr and nonzero exit. Establish practical word tokenization (Unicode letters/digits with apostrophes perhaps) and document intended behavior back to me. Do not edit README or tests.
sessions.result:
Implemented `wordfreq.js` and `package.json`, including the `npm test` script.

Tokenization uses Unicode letters and numbers, preserving straight or curly apostrophes only when they join alphanumeric parts. Words are case-insensitive; results sort by frequency descending, then alphabetically. The CLI supports `--min-length` (default `1`), reports validation and usage errors to stderr, and exits nonzero on errors.

Files changed: `wordfreq.js`, `package.json`.

sessions.brief: Create tests using node:test for expected wordfreq behavior. Own test files only (e.g. test/wordfreq.test.js); do not edit package.json, implementation, or README. Test frequency ordering/tie handling/case normalization/tokenization and CLI input/error behavior as feasible; assume executable/source will be wordfreq.js and package script may run node --test. Report assumptions and test command.
sessions.result:
Created `test/wordfreq.test.js` and `test/sample.txt`. The tests cover frequency ordering and ties, case normalization, tokenization, top-N limiting, `--min-length` defaults and filtering, and CLI errors.

Assumptions: output is `word count` per line; ties sort alphabetically; tokens support Unicode letters/numbers and internal apostrophes. `node --test test/wordfreq.test.js` passes. Full `node --test` also discovers a root-level test whose option-order assertion fails; I did not edit that file.
